{{short description|Concept in category theory (in mathematics)}}
In [[Abstract algebra|algebra]], the '''coimage''' of a [[homomorphism]]

:<math>f : A \rightarrow B</math>

is the [[quotient group|quotient]]

:<math>\text{coim} f = A/\ker(f)</math>

of the [[domain of a function|domain]] by the [[kernel (algebra)|kernel]]. 
The coimage is [[natural isomorphism|canonically isomorphic]] to the [[image (mathematics)|image]] by the [[isomorphism theorem|first isomorphism theorem]], when that theorem applies.

More generally, in [[category theory]], the '''coimage''' of a [[morphism]] is the dual notion of the [[image (category theory)|image of a morphism]]. If  <math>f : X \rightarrow Y</math>, then a coimage of <math>f</math>  (if it exists) is an [[epimorphism]] <math>c : X \rightarrow C</math> such that
#there is a map <math>f_c : C \rightarrow Y </math> with <math> f =f_c \circ c </math>,
#for any epimorphism <math>z : X \rightarrow Z</math> for which there is a map <math>f_z : Z \rightarrow Y </math> with <math> f =f_z \circ z </math>, there is a unique map <math> h : Z \rightarrow C </math> such that both <math> c =h \circ z </math> and <math> f_z =f_c \circ h </math>
